visuals.summary: 1: A grey field of square tiles with the word WORDLE printed in letterspaced capitals across its middle row. A logo-style banner, not a plot: no axes, no data, no legend.
1: Two rows of five cells. Header row: Original data | marxh(473) | tash(314) | clen(525) | rprobe(545) | 2569(529). Second row: Data after cleaning | marsh | trash | clean | probe | 25569.

2: A three-column flowchart titled 1.4 Our Work. Left box GRU Prediction Model: input, then a GRU model block with curved arrows labelled reset gate and update gate, then output, then prediction, then March 1, 2023. Middle column Relationship of Word Attributes and Scores from Percentage: the score equation is printed inside the box, then two branches, Regression Analysis (fword and fLetter leading to Regression analysis) and Box Plot Analysis (rep and pos leading to three labelled output cells, Box length difference, Number difference of outliers, Median difference), each branch ending in a tick except the pos branch which ends in a cross; a right-hand label reads err. Below, a large dashed box GRU Pridiction Model holds input, a Grid Search box labelled best params, a March 1 2023 / EERIE block, a Random Forest block, prediction and output. Right column Interesting Features of Data: Word Attributes leading to not linearly related and no obvious diff, both fed from Hard Mode Percentage, and The most hellish level:PARER leading to hard to guess. Bottom right, Difficulty Rate Classification Model by K-Means++: the difficulty-rate equation is printed inside the box, then Difficulty Rate delta, then K-Means++ Clustering Analysis and Difficulty classification feeding a stack of levels that points at EERIE.

2: One unlabelled two-column block. Rows: score | the combination of the percentage of scores. fword | the word frequency. fLetter | the letter frequency. rep | the repetition of word. pos | the part of speech of word. sigma | the difficulty rate. MSE | the Mean Squared Error. MAE | the Mean Absolute Error. d | the Euclidean distance. SSE | the Sum of Squared Errors.

3: A small algorithm-flow diagram above the update equations, drawn in the same house style as Figure 2: a block sequence with arrows and no data, no axes, and no values. The paper's prose on page 8 reads this flowchart as if it were the deviation plot of Figure 4.

3: Two-column glossary for equation (1). Symbol column and a Decription column (spelled that way in the header). Rows: h(t-1) | the hidden state at time t - 1 or at time 0; h-tilde(t) | the new candidate hidden state; sigma | the sigmoid function; * | the Hadamard product; x(t) | the input; W_ir, W_hr, W_iz, W_hz, W_in, W_hn | the parameters that need to be trained; b_ir, b_hr, b_iz, b_hz, b_in, b_hn | the parameters that need to be trained.

4: A deviation plot over the test window: a line of relative error against time, sitting low across the year with one spike to about 50% at the Christmas point. The y-axis carries the deviation in percent; the caption supplies the definition rather than an axis label. This is the figure the prose on the same page calls Figure 3.
4: One data row under six headers: x-bar(t) | x-hat-bar(t) | Relative error | Relative error rate | RMSE | Relative RESE. Values: 24956.1667 | 25494.4569 | 538.29019 | 2.1569% | 1621.0881 | 6.4957%.

5: A compact overview diagram of section 5's route, drawn in the house style of Figure 2: a box for word frequency and letter frequency feeding a regression branch, and rep and pos feeding a comparison branch, with tick and cross marks for the kept and dropped attributes. No axes, no values.

6: Two scatter panels side by side, both with the vertical axis labelled y(log10) and the horizontal axis in frequency units. Panel (a) Word frequency: cloud of points across roughly 0.10 to 0.25 on the horizontal axis with a fitted line sloping down, y values spanning about 1.7 to 2.2. Panel (b) Letter frequency: the same construction, horizontal axis labelled Letter frequency. Both panels are described in the prose as having empty lower-left and upper-right corners.
5: Three-column table. Header: Regression with score | Pearson | Spearman. Rows: Word frequency | -0.3165 | -0.3256. Letter frequency | -0.4238 | -0.4005.

7: Two panels. Panel (a) Boxplot of repetition: two boxes, With repetition and Without repetition, on a vertical axis running about 1.6 to 2.4, with a handful of outlier points above each. Panel (b) Density of repetition: two overlaid density curves, legend With repetition and Without repetition, horizontal axis carrying score values around 1.4, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0, 2.2.
6: Three headers, Median difference | Box length difference | Number difference of outliers, with one value printed under the first two: 0.130037 and 0.00556. The third column carries no value.

8: Two panels arranged in the same style as Figure 7 but with a 2x2 layout underneath: (a) Boxplot of POS with four boxes labelled Noun, Adjective, Adverb, verb on a vertical axis about 1.6 to 2.3, and (b) Density of POS with four overlapping density curves and a legend reading Adjective, Adverb, Noun, verb.

7: Four headers, Median difference1 | Median difference2 | Median difference3, with three values: 0.024991 | -0.05973 | -0.05972. The first header is run together with its numeral while the second and third are not spaced consistently.

9: A wide algorithm flowchart in the house style: a Gridsearch block on the left, then best hparams, then a Random forest block fed by subsample 1 through subsample n and labelled Training Set, whose output trees vote through CLASSA, CLASSA, CLASS M and a final CLASS cell. No axes and no values.
8: One data row under three headers. Headers: fword, | fLetter, | ref. Values: 0.00023% | 0.418799 | 1.5.
9: One row under five headers. Headers: max depth, | max features, | min samples leaf | min samples split | n estimators. Values: 10 | sqrt | 2 | 10 | 200.

10: One row of seven percentages under the bin headers 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | X. Values: 1.07508% | 6.51769% | 23.30265% | 30.29725% | 23.13552% | 13.27519% | 2.40859%. A second line under the row reads MSE: 20.70641 and MAE: 3.24388.

10: Two panels, (a) and (b), both untitled beyond the letters. Panel (a) shows the word EERIE placed against a vertical difficulty scale running 0.0 to 0.8. Panel (b) shows the clustering of words by difficulty against the same kind of scale. The axes carry no titles; the values are legible only as ticks.

11: Two scatter panels in the same style as Figure 6, (a) Word frequency and (b) Letter frequency, each against the daily Hard Mode percentage on the vertical axis running about 0.10 to 0.12, with a horizontal axis carrying frequency values 0.10 through 0.55. The clouds are flat: the prose reads them as showing no relationship.

12: A four-panel figure lettered (a) Boxplot of repetition, (b) Density of repetition, (c) Boxplot of POS, (d) Density of POS, arranged two by two. Panels (a) and (b) carry one box or two density curves labelled With repetition and without repetition; panels (c) and (d) carry four boxes labelled Noun, Adjective, Adverb, verb and four density curves. Vertical axes for the POS panels run about 0.02 to 0.12.
13: Two cropped screenshots of social media posts, labelled (a) User comment1[9] and (b) User comment2[10]. Both are images of text, not plots; the words inside them are the only content.

14: Two panels (a) and (b). Panel (a) plots density curves overlaid with a legend reading original data and a second entry for the perturbed series, against vertical axis bins labelled 1 try, 2 tries, 3 tries, 6 tries. Panel (b) shows the same comparison in the other representation. No numeric axis values are printed for the density.
15: Two panels (a) and (b) in the same construction as Figure 14, with the category axis carrying all six and the X bin labels, 1 try through 6 tries plus the original data legend entry.
